Aer Lingus: sandwiches; snacks; treats; drinks; complimentary meals on transatlantic flights
Air Canada: International economy passengers receive complimentary meals including a salad, warm bread, a hot entrée and dessert, plus a light meal or hot snack before landing. New offerings include red Thai chicken and rice, chicken cacciatore with roast potatoes and bell peppers, and pesto penne, as well as a pancake and maple syrup breakfast on longer flights. Monty’s Bakehouse savoury pastries (coconut chicken and potato sour cream & chive) and appetisers like soba noodles, chaat, hummus and vegetables are available. The buy‑on‑board Bistro menu features peppercorn roast beef sandwiches, cheeseburger sliders and Mediterranean hummus wraps. Snacks include herb and garlic pretzels, candy mix, Chomps beef jerky and Ghirardelli dark chocolate squares, and there is an expanded tea selection.
Air France: starter; choice of two hot dishes; bread; cheese; dessert; hot beverages; cold beverages; wine; champagne; Long‑haul economy meals include a starter, choice of two hot dishes, bread and cheese, dessert, and hot or cold beverages including wine and champagne; passengers can enjoy beverages and a box of sweet and savoury treats (cereal bars, mini sandwiches) throughout the flight and receive a snack or breakfast before arrival. Short‑ and medium‑haul flights offer a sweet or savoury snack; flights longer than 1.55 h include a sweet snack plus fresh sandwich, and those over 2.30 h have a meal box with three sandwiches (two vegetarian).
British Airways: starter; main; dessert; hot drinks; cold drinks; alcoholic drinks; mid-flight snacks; second meal on longer flights; Economy (World Traveller) passengers receive a starter, main dish and dessert with a choice of hot, cold or alcoholic drinks; on long flights there are mid‑flight snacks and a second meal before landing. On short‑haul flights, food is available from the High Life Café, which sells sweet and savoury snacks.
Delta Air Lines: Complimentary snacks (Cheez‑It crackers, Lotus Biscoff cookies, chocolate chip granola bars, SunChips) are available in all cabins; for purchase: snack boxes (Bistro box with potato chips, crackers, cheese spread, beef snack stick, almonds, chocolate cookies, gummy bears; Market box with pita chips, hummus, olives, dried fruit, almonds, ginger chew); individual snacks such as Dot’s Pretzels, Nerds Gummy Clusters, Pringles. On longer flights passengers can buy fresh plates such as a chicken salad sandwich plate or fruit & cheese plate. Beverages include a variety of soft drinks, juices, Starbucks coffee, tea, bottled water and alcoholic drinks (beer, wines, rum, gin, bourbon, whiskey, tequila and vodka).
Emirates: multicourse meal; main course; fresh fruit or salad; crackers and cheese; sweet treat; fruit juices; soft drinks; wines; beers; spirits; Economy passengers receive two hot meals on long‑haul flights, with multi‑course service that includes fresh fruit, a dessert, crackers and cheese. There is a wide selection of complimentary wines, beers and spirits; special meals (e.g., gluten‑friendly or low‑lactose) are available. Passengers can purchase Moët & Chandon champagne or celebration cakes and may request extra portions if available.
Finnair: On long‑haul flights economy passengers receive a hot meal with non‑alcoholic beverages plus one complimentary glass of wine or a mild alcoholic drink, and a second light meal or snack before landing; additional food and drinks can be purchased via the Nordic Sky portal. On European flights, paid options include instant Asian chicken noodles and creamy pesto pasta, warm tomato & spinach lasagna and green chicken curry, as well as a selection of soft drinks, smoothies, energy drinks, beer, wine, spirits, coffee, tea and hot chocolate. Complimentary blueberry juice or water is offered, and decaf coffee is available upon request.
Iberia: On flights over 4.5 hours economy passengers are served breakfast, lunch and/or dinner with vegetarian options; on shorter flights they can buy a selection of sweet and savoury snacks from the Gastrobar. Passengers may also pre‑order menus featuring fresh products such as vegan and salmon poke bowls, salads, pasta dishes, burgers and desserts. A wide range of special meals is available, including vegetarian, low‑fat, low‑lactose, low‑salt, diabetic, gluten‑free and children’s meals; flights to or from Doha exclude pork and alcohol.
KLM: warm dish; large salad; dessert; vegetarian options; drinks; coffee or tea; snack or sandwich on flights longer than 10 hours; Snacks and drink on short European flights; fresh sandwiches, often vegetarian, on longer European flights; intercontinental flights provide a warm dish with choice, a large salad, dessert, vegetarian options, a bottle of water, and drinks with coffee or tea; snacks or a warm sandwich are served before landing.
Lufthansa: menus; snacks; soft drinks; alcoholic beverages; special meals; country-specific cuisine on some international routes; Lufthansa’s long‑haul service features the ‘Sky Selection’ of tapas bowls, currywurst and macarons, alongside three hot main course options and fresh bread for premium economy. Economy passengers on flights over ten hours are offered three hot main course options as part of a revamped service. Business‑class style appetisers and breakfast options such as smoothies, French toast and omelettes are available in higher classes.
Qatar Airways: destination-inspired meals; freshly prepared meals; expertly selected beverages; special meals; children meals; all meals halal; Economy breakfast on long‑haul flights may include a croissant, strawberry yoghurt, sliced fruit and orange juice, alongside a cheese omelet with hash brown, cooked tomato, mushrooms and chicken sausage. Alternative options include pancakes or an Indian vegetarian breakfast.
Ryanair: meal deal; soft drinks; snacks; hot drinks; beer; spirits; wine; prosecco; confectionery; The Getaway Café offers meal deals (e.g., three‑cheese toastie, hot bacon baguette, hot ham & cheese panini, hot chicken seeded panini or a premium fresh sandwich) with a drink and snack. Beverages include tea, Lavazza coffee, hot chocolate, soft drinks, beer, wine, prosecco and spirits. Snacks include crisps and pretzels, Pringles, peanuts, M&M’s, Maltesers, stroopwafels, Haribo, KitKat, Kinder Bueno, Twix, Snickers, Skittles, Walkers Shortbread and chocolate croissants.
SAS: The ‘Flavors by SAS’ concept (introduced in 2025) offers globally inspired cuisine with tiered service levels, from simple baskets to full tray meals containing hot and cold dishes. Menus rotate and feature flavours from Europe, the U.S., Asia, the Middle East and the Mediterranean, allowing SAS to adjust meals based on flight time and route.
TUI Airways: hot snacks; cold snacks; drinks; hot food; sandwiches; main meal on long-haul flights; light snack before landing
Transavia: hot snacks; sandwiches; soft drinks; juices; sweet gluten-free snacks; savoury gluten-free snacks; alcoholic drinks; The menu structure is similar to other low‑cost carriers: service begins with coffee or tea and something sweet, then offers fresh sandwiches, hot snacks and soup, followed by salty and sweet snacks, alcoholic drinks and cold beverages.
Turkish Airlines: hot breakfast; cold breakfast; hot meal; cold meal; egg options; natural muesli; cheeses; regional appetizers; pasta alternatives; grilled dishes; snacks; Economy long‑haul meals include dishes such as chicken satay (kebabs) with green salad, hummus and fig chocolate mousse, served with hot bread. Snacks in the galley may include cheese sandwiches and cherry cake, and a second meal prior to landing may feature Greek salad, macaroni noodles in bolognese sauce and apricot mousse.
United Airlines: Short‑haul flights (300–500 miles) provide free snacks with alcoholic drinks for purchase. Flights over 500 miles offer premium snacks and Bistro on Board fresh meals for purchase in addition to free snacks. On international flights to Asia, Europe or South America, economy passengers receive a complimentary bread roll, salad, main entree and dessert, a free mid‑flight sandwich on flights over 12 hours, and a pre‑arrival meal; beer and wine are free. Passengers can pre‑order fresh meals such as the Steakhouse Burger, Tacos Al Pastor, Fresh Cheese & Fruit Tray and Everything Bagel Dots, and new menu options will include salads and gourmet sandwiches and wraps.
easyJet: Costa coffee; fresh sandwiches; hot meals; snacks; meal deals; Onboard menu includes Costa coffee, fresh sandwiches, hot meals and snacks delivered to passengers’ seats; meal deals combine a main, drink and snack. The menu progression starts with coffee or tea and something sweet, followed by fresh sandwiches, hot snacks and soup, then salty and sweet snacks, alcoholic drinks and cold beverages.
